article.title: BDS at 20: activists confront European complicity at Barcelona conference
article.author: Ana Vračar
article.content: “This is a European issue because Europe is a partner in crime,” co-founder of the Boycott, Divestment, Sanctions (BDS) movement Omar Barghouti said on the opening day of a conference marking the movement’s 20th anniversary in Barcelona. “Most of the governments, the corporations, the institutions, the universities, your so-called media, many of them are partners in crimes. They’re complicit in Israel’s regime of genocide, apartheid, occupation – and they have been for quite some time.” Hundreds of people attended the opening night of the BDS conference in Barcelona on November 18. Source: BreakThrough News The BDS campaign has seen a notable surge in Europe since the beginning of the genocide in Gaza, supported by diverse groups, from trade unions to left political parties. “This campaign is important to confront apartheid, militarization, and genocide,” general secretary of the Workers’ Party of Belgium (PTB-PVDA) Peter Mertens told BreakThrough News at the opening. “It means working towards a future against the war machine. Defeat the war machine, defeat genocide, defeat apartheid – this will liberate not only Palestine, but all of us.” The three-day event, taking place through November 20 under the theme “Resisting Might-Makes-Right: for Palestine, for Humanity,” is organized by the Palestinian BDS National Committee (BNC), including the Palestinian Campaign for the Academic and Cultural Boycott of Israel (PACBI), in cooperation with European partners. Hundreds of people joined the launch event on November 18. Barghouti spoke alongside UN Special Rapporteur Francesca Albanese , surgeon Ghassan Abu-Sittah, actress Hiba Abouk, and former Colombian energy minister Andrés Camacho. Later sessions featured human rights attorney Noura Erakat , writer Fatima Bhutto, and trade unionist Zita Holbourne, among others. BDS actions as “lights piercing the darkness of European complicity and repression” Offering a glimpse into upcoming days of strategizing and exchange by Palestine solidarity activists, the opening speakers took stock of Europe’s ongoing complicity in Israeli crimes – and of the breakthroughs achieved through BDS initiatives across the region. The movement has undeniably grown since 2023. Groups are campaigning against tech companies that fuel the genocide while embedding themselves in European public and security services. Cultural , academic, and sports boycott campaigns have expanded alongside them. Dockworkers blocked arms shipments to Israel, and students launched dozens of encampments against their universities’ cooperation with the occupation’s institutions. Read more: BDS movement makes significant strides across Europe These actions, Barghouti said, “are some of those many beautiful European lights that are shining and piercing the darkness of European complicity and repression.” “The Gaza genocide has become the litmus test by which people test the moral fabric of individuals, pop stars, and politicians,” Abu-Sittah emphasized, adding that the tone and strength of recent student demonstrations represented another achievement. Read more: Israeli destruction of Gaza’s healthcare is a blueprint for future imperialist wars “There is a generation that is formatively and structurally aware of the relationship between capitalist austerity that is destroying the lives of the people in the core of the empire and capitalist colonialism that is consuming the lives of Palestinians in Gaza through a system that also creates profit,” he said. “These cannibalistic classes of Western colonialism that consume the lives of the poor and the superfluous populations in Europe, in North America, are the cannibalistic classes that consume the lives of the children and the Palestinian civilians inside Gaza.” International law is still relevant Yet European countries continue to conduct business as usual and maintain partnerships with the occupation power, Barghouti argued, with the regional far right enthusiastically joining the drive despite its own antisemitic character. “Israel sells its military technologies as ‘battle tested’ and extensively uses bribery, bullying and extortion of elected officials including through ‘private Mossad companies,” he insisted. “Israel exports weaponized spyware and has used this information in election rigging services to influence elections in Slovenia , France, NYC, and possibly in Colombia and Brazil.” Opening speakers included Omar Barghouti, Francesca Albanese, Ghassan Abu-Sittah, Hiba Abouk, Andrés Camacho, and many more. Source: BreakThrough News In such a context, Francesca Albanese said during a press conference ahead of the launch, many ask if international law is still relevant. “Oh, yes, it is very relevant.” Instruments like the UN Charter, the Universal Declaration of Human Rights, and the Refugee Convention, she added, “exist to protect humanity from war, persecution, and extermination.” “I agree that the system that was conceived 80 years ago was still bearing the colonial imprint of the countries who composed the international community back then, and that we are still fighting to undo that colonial legacy. That system has not led us to heaven, but has saved us – until now – from hell.” Palestinians are calling for meaningful solidarity, not charity “International law, as we understand it, was established in order to facilitate relationships between imperial powers as they expanded their hold on the globe, its resources, and its people,” added Noura Erakat. “It was because of the Third World revolt that we saw these laws transform in order to serve us and to serve the salt of this earth.” “And so we – as those in the Third World tradition have always done – retool these tools that are meant to suppress us and to maintain the structure of domination, in order to advance justice on behalf of the people. At this moment, it is not what international law says about Palestine, but rather what Palestine says about international law and its legitimacy.” Read more: Romania: a growing hub of complicity in genocide “To resist this [might-makes-right] order, Palestinians have a near consensus in our demand to the global solidarity movement,” Barghouti said. “One, uplift the inalienable right of our people under international law, at the very least an end to the occupation, end to apartheid, and right of refugees to return and to reparations. And two, end all forms of complicity in Israeli crimes, especially through BDS.” “Palestinians are not calling for charity. We are calling for meaningful solidarity.”
